messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Elevated token-error rate and KV cache memory growth on prod-west-1. Triggered by continuous-batching component. Auto-escalation to oncall.

mike: I’m oncall, looking at metrics now. seeing 3x increase in avg batch size and KV cache resident set growing fast. errors are mostly "kv_miss_replay" and occasional OOMs on worker-12.

sara: same dashboard — draft/target sync mismatch spikes coincide with speculative decode toggles. suspect interaction between speculative decoding + prefix/KV caching.

alan: confirm logs show many speculative drafts being materialized into KV cache entries that later diverge. that would amplify cache churn under continuous batching.

mike: first mitigation: throttle continuous-batching to target 50ms max batch window and drop speculative decoding to false for model-group `redwood-opt-13b` in prod-west-1.

sara: commands I’ll run in config service (prod):
```bash
# reduce batch window
curl -s -X POST https://config.prod.redwood/api/v1/overrides \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN' \n  -d '{"component":"continuous_batching","region":"prod-west-1","max_batch_window_ms":50}'

# disable speculative decoding for the model group
curl -s -X POST https://config.prod.redwood/api/v1/overrides \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN' \n  -d '{"component":"speculative_decoder","region":"prod-west-1","model_group":"redwood-opt-13b","enabled":false}'
```

ops-bot: deployment event logged: config-override/1851234567 applied by sara. rollout in progress (canary 10% -> 50%).

julie: heads-up: support has reports from enterprise-cust-42 and dev-platform-alpha about latency spikes and a few 5xxs. customer impact: degraded latencies (~+180ms p50) and ~4% increase in 5xxs during peak. notified account teams.

mike: rolling the canary now, watching latency, error rate, and KV resident size. if resident set drops and 5xxs decline, escalate to full rollout.

sara: quick sanity check on cache keys: many keys include speculative draft tokens suffix, e.g., `ctx:<user>:<prefix>|draft:<spec_id>`. that's the divergence source. we should stop caching speculative drafts or separate them into ephemeral cache with short TTL.

alan: agree. short-term: treat speculative entries as non-evictable? no — that would worsen. short TTL (5s) + do not include speculative flag in primary KV key. medium-term: change sync protocol so speculative drafts don't write into main KV unless stabilized.

mike: can we patch runtime now? risky. prefer config toggles. current plan: (1) finish canary for config disabling speculative decoding; (2) reduce batch window; (3) if improvement, push global override; (4) schedule postmortem and engineering task for spec-draft cache model.

ops-bot: canary metrics: at 60s after change p50 latency -100ms, 5xx rate -2.6%, KV resident set -32% on worker cohort.

julie: support confirms customer errors are decreasing for enterprise-cust-42. account alerted that mitigation is in flight. thanks.

mike: proceeding to global rollout -> applying config to all prod regions. will keep one region as control for 10m.

sara: leaving a trace snippet for engineers investigating divergence:
```text
// observed pattern in logs
[spec_decision] req=abcd123 draft_id=dft-9f8 created=2025-11-03T14:03:12Z
[kv_write] key=ctx:usr:42|draft:dft-9f8 size=1.2KB ttl=3600
[batch_commit] batch=873 size=78 spec_included=true
[reconcile] req=abcd123 target_root=rt-7f6 mismatch=true -> replay
```

alan: adding note: speculative decoding increases duplicate state written to KV when drafts diverge later. continuous batching aggregates many requests and amplifies the number of writes per second which can cause cache blowup under churn.

mike: global rollout completed at last_message_ts 1851234899. Post-rollout quick checks look good. No further OOMs. Creating follow-up issues:
- SRE: Add emergency toggle runbook for speculative-decoding interactions with KV cache.
- Eng-ML: Task to separate speculative draft keys into ephemeral cache and reduce TTL.
- Eng-runtime: Evaluate batch-window heuristics to detect cache-churn and auto-throttle.

julie: handoff to daytime oncall (alan) for follow-ups and postmortem. adding timeline and links to ticket.

alan: acknowleged, will own postmortem + mitigation design docs. thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident severity updated to SEV-2 (mitigated) | created incident ticket INC-2025-1083 | timeline recorded.
